claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide covers how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi programs.

The Pulumi Terraform provider SDK (`@pulumi/terraform`) exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource class that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference a Terraform state file stored in S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` instances expose a `getOutput(name)` method that returns the named output from the referenced Terraform state.
The `terraform.state.S3Reference` class is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` when importing from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.

`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves the `vpcId` output from another Pulumi stack named `core-infra` (StackReference name given without org/project qualification).
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` (value "DEFAULT") properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred from Terraform to Pulumi gradually, resource-by-resource, during migration.

The `pulumi import` CLI takes arguments in the form `<type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, and these `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` type tokens are valid.
There is a 'Pulumi import API' that can be used programmatically within a TypeScript program to import resources.
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; a policy pack's policies take `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` with callback signature `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can take values `public-read` and `public-read-write`.
The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Automation API (`@pulumi/pulumi/automation`) provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({stackName, projectName, program})`, `stack.setConfig(key, {value})`, and `stack.up({onOutput})` returning a result with `.outputs`.

Component resources can wrap Terraform-state-backed infrastructure so that developers create components in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
Custom component resources extend `pulumi.ComponentResource` and call `super("custom:WebApplication", name, {}, opts)` with a type token, and register outputs via `this.registerOutputs`.
`aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` with Fargate accepts `cpu: "256"` and `memory: "512"`, and `aws.ecs.Service` `networkConfiguration` accepts `assignPublicIp: true` and `subnets`.
